item.title: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players”
item.description: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players” Alongside her strong form at Angel City and her string of call-ups to the Brazilian national team, motherhood has brought a new chapter to Ary Borges’ journey. At a press conference on Thursday (26), the midfielder highlighted the support she received from head coach Arthur Elias and spoke about the importance of his understanding when he left her out of October’s international window so she could spend the first days of her newborn daughter Melanie’s life alongside her wife, Gabriela. “This is a very special time for me. Arthur is a very caring person who really values relationships, both individually and as a group. In this situation, he showed once again how much he stands by us and understands the players. Arthur watched me grow at Centro Olímpico, and now he has watched me become a mother,” she said. “Before the last squad announcement, he called me, asked about my family and was very honest with me. He said that my saying no at that moment (to joining the squad) was actually saying yes. As athletes, we give up so much, and he gave me peace of mind to enjoy a special moment with my family. He also reassured other players who want to become mothers but worry it could affect their careers,” she added. Ary Borges during a Brazilian women’s national team training session in Hiroshima, Japan Credit: Luciana Vermell/CBF Ary has known Arthur Elias since her days at Centro Olímpico, where she played between 2015 and 2016. As a youngster, she would talk with her teammates about the possibility of being a ball girl at matches involving the team he coached. Years later, he would become her coach with the Brazilian national team and her nemesis in matches between Corinthians and Palmeiras, as she played for Palmeiras from 2020 to 2022, during a period of Corinthians dominance. Among the players called up for this international window, Ary logged the most playing time for her club, Angel City in the United States. She made 28 appearances and played 2,688 minutes, figures that underline her consistent involvement throughout the season. Speaking about the challenges facing Brazil in Japan, the midfielder highlighted the importance of the friendlies against the hosts as part of their World Cup preparations. “We’re very happy to be here in Japan and experience a different culture. Our profession gives us that privilege. In football terms, Japan are opponents who present us with plenty of challenges. This is another opportunity for us to study, improve and work toward our main goal, which is getting closer and closer (the World Cup). These have all the makings of two very interesting games, and I hope that, just like last time, we come away with two wins,” she said. item.title: Rams grind out 26-13 win over Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
item.description: Nov 25, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images INGLEWOOD, Calif. — Blake Corum turned 26 on Wednesday and celebrated with a career-best performance, carrying the ball 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams controlled the clock and the trenches in a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers . It was the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the Rams used it to extend their winning streak to five and improve to 7-4. Corum’s 32 carries were the most by a Rams running back in Sean McVay’s decade in charge. He scored for the seventh straight game, and Kyren Williams added a touchdown and 46 yards on 12 carries as Los Angeles finished with 241 rushing yards. Brandon McManus contributed four field goals. Matthew Stafford needed only 16 completions on 23 attempts for 140 yards (and one interception) as the Rams leaned on the ground game against an injury-thinned receiving corps. The teams were tied 13-13 at halftime. Green Bay had clawed back from an early deficit behind a Christian Watson touchdown catch, but the second half belonged entirely to the Rams. Los Angeles outscored the Packers 13-0 after the break, held Green Bay to just 55 rushing yards, and dominated time of possession (40:40 to 19:20). Jordan Love finished 17-of-29 for 198 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. The Packers fell to 6-5 after their second straight loss. The night was not without controversy. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson late in the second quarter; Watson was ruled out with a concussion after catching four passes for 65 yards and the score. Micah Parsons, returning from a torn ACL, recorded a sack for Green Bay, but the Packers could not generate consistent offense once the Rams established their rushing rhythm. The result carries clear playoff weight. Both teams entered at 6-4 in a crowded NFC wild-card race; the head-to-head win and the possession edge now give the Rams a clearer path. Los Angeles hosts the Kansas City Chiefs next, while Green Bay travels to face the New Orleans Saints.

item.title: Jackson’s Future In Miami Looks Grim Despite Sunday’s Start
item.description: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins are staring down a massive decision at right tackle, and the writing is on the wall for Austin Jackson. Yahoo Sports NFL reports that Jackson is in the last year of his contract while the coaching staff actively weighs a change at the position. This is a bad week and likely the end of his time in South Florida. Proctor Stays Put for Now While some reports suggest Proctor is the heir apparent to the right tackle spot, Head Coach Jeff Hafley shut down that talk before practice on Wednesday. Per Sports Illustrated , Proctor will not be moving to right tackle this week and might not make the switch at all this season. The team is sticking with Jackson for now, barring an injury that forces him out of the upcoming game against the New York Jets. Hafley did not say exactly what is wrong with Jackson, only that the player would be limited in practice on Wednesday. The coach added that Jackson is expected to line up at his spot at right tackle when the Jets visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday. This leaves the Dolphins in a weird spot, relying on a player who has struggled all season while holding a rookie guard back from his natural progression. Looking Beyond the Current Roster The front office is clearly weighing long-term options while trying to win the next game. If the team moves on from Jackson, they have seen other players step up elsewhere in the league. Chukwuebuka Godrick started three games for the Kansas City Chiefs last season, and Caedan Wallace has two career starts on his resume with the New England Patriots. Wallace started one game at left tackle and the other as a sixth offensive lineman, showing he can handle different roles. The Dolphins also have a pass rush to worry about on the other side of the ball. Rookie pass rusher David Bailey is the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft and is tied for third in the NFL with 9.5 sacks. During their first meeting in Week 7, the Dolphins limited him to four tackles and half a sack over 61 snaps, with Bailey recording those statistics. The team faces the Jets this Sunday at 1 p.m.

item.title: Detroit Tigers Sign Two Familiar Faces
item.description: The Detroit Tigers are bringing back a pair of familiar faces just one week after parting ways with them. According to Tigers beat writer Evan Woodbery of MLive, the organization has signed infielder Trey Sweeney and left-handed pitcher Jake Miller to minor-league contracts after non-tendering both players last week. The moves allow Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris to retain both players without committing spots on the 40-man roster. It is a strategy that has become somewhat familiar during Harris’ tenure in Detroit. Sep 23, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Detroit Tigers shortstop Trey Sweeney (27) throws to first in the third inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Tigers Re-Sign Trey Sweeney and Jake Miller Both signings are confirmed on the Tigers’ official transaction page , which lists the moves as taking place on November 25. Sweeney and Miller had been among the four players Detroit designated for assignment on November 17 before officially becoming free agents. Sweeney, 26, provides the Tigers with additional infield depth as he works to reestablish himself following an injury-plagued 2026 campaign. Although there is no guarantee he will return to the major league roster, keeping him in the organization makes sense for Detroit. Meanwhile, Miller, 25, is an intriguing left-handed pitching prospect who missed a significant portion of last season with a hip injury. According to NBC Sports , Miller posted a 0.77 ERA and struck out 24 batters across 23 1/3 minor-league innings in 2026. Scott Harris Continues Familiar Roster-Building Strategy As Woodbery pointed out Thursday morning, Harris has had considerable success convincing players who have been non-tendered to return to the Tigers on minor-league contracts. The strategy allows Detroit to retain organizational depth while maintaining flexibility on its 40-man roster. Sweeney and Miller were two of the three players the Tigers non-tendered ahead of last week’s deadline , with outfielder Matt Vierling being the other. Whether Vierling could eventually return to the organization remains to be seen. Neither signing is going to generate the excitement of a major free-agent acquisition, but these are the types of low-risk moves that can pay dividends over the course of a 162-game season. In Miller’s case, particularly, there is enough upside to make bringing him back a worthwhile investment.

item.title: WNBA’s 2027 Cap Math Leaves Little Room For Error For Dream
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The WNBA salary cap rules for 2027 create a harsh reality for teams trying to build a winner. The Atlanta Dream faces a math problem that leaves almost no room for maneuvering. According to Sports Illustrated , the league cap can rise by no more than 13% to $7.91 million. This small jump does not help teams that already have limited space. The Dream must sign three new players just to fill their roster. Each of these new signings costs at least $280,800. That adds up fast and eats into the money available for star talent. The Minimum Salary Trap Every team must keep 12 players on the roster during the season. This rule forces franchises to spend money they might prefer to save. Per Sports Illustrated, the lowest full-season minimum salary for a player with no experience is $280,800 in 2027. The Dream already has nine players under contract totaling about $6.18 million. To reach the required 12 players, the team needs to spend an extra $842,400 on new signings. This mandatory spending pushes their total obligations to $7.02 million. The math leaves the team with very little flexibility to sign big free agents. Where the Money Goes The gap between the total cap and what a team can actually spend is now wider than ever. The Atlanta Dream will have to spend $7.02 million just to meet basic roster requirements. This leaves them with about $886,000 to spend freely on top-tier talent. That amount is tiny compared to the cost of a supermax deal. A supermax salary is 20% of the cap for a given year, which would be roughly $1.58 million. Only the current club or, in the event of free agency, the former club can sign an eligible player to a supermax. This restriction makes it hard for other teams to poach stars from the Dream without paying a premium. Spending Limits and Roster Rules A team’s payroll cannot surpass the salary cap at any moment unless it applies a hardship, emergency hardship, pregnancy/childbirth, or season-ending injury exception. For any specific year, the standard maximum salary equals 17% of the salary cap. These tight limits mean teams cannot simply throw money at every problem. They must plan carefully or risk breaking the rules. The Dream’s situation shows how the new rules squeeze out spending power. With only $886,000 left for free spending, the team has very few options to improve the roster beyond the minimums. The Dream, in its present form, must spend $7.02 million, which leaves approximately $886,000 available for unrestricted spending above minimum salaries.

item.title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
item.description: Detroit Lions fans dress for Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears, Thursday, Nov. 28, 2019 at Ford Field. Detroit Lions fans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary. (He was a driving force behind other innovations like instant replay, the flags on goal posts, the NFL-AFL merger, and too many others to name). He jumped at the opportunity. The Cowboys hosted their first Thanksgiving game in 1966. They kept the game annually until the 1970’s when the league hatched a plan to alternate between the Cowboys and the then St. Louis Cardinals . The Cowboys were to host the second game in even years and the Cardinals in odd years. The Cardinals only hosted two home Thanksgiving games, however, which took place in 1975 and in 1977. item.title: Christian Pulisic, Antoine Griezmann and Emma Hayes’ USWNT: Why American soccer fans have plenty to celebrate this Thanksgiving
item.description: Thanksgiving 2026 GFX - GOAL GOAL breaks down what you should be thankful for during this holiday season. It's Thanksgiving, and we all know what that means. Turkey, gravy, mashed potatoes, stuffing - all on the menu. There's plenty to be thankful for, but that doesn't just extend to food; it extends to soccer, too. Obviously, there are more important things in life to give thanks for at this time of year, but it is also worth acknowledging the sport's role in everyday life. For some, it's an obsession. For others, it's a distraction. But, if you're reading this story, it's safe to assume that you're glad that soccer is a part of your life in some way. So, with that in mind, let's sit down, put down the fork for a moment and give thanks for all of the good things about American soccer and, just as crucially, all of the things worth being excited for on the horizon, too. The 2026 World Cup Spain helped make the 2026 World Cup a summer to remember as fans from across the globe came together in America. Yeah, it's over now, but what a ride it was! For one summer, soccer came stateside and, for one summer, America was at the forefront of the beautiful game. The scenes were unforgettable: the games, the pageantry, the fans sweeping through cities. Scotland in Boston, Algeria in Kansas, Norway's Viking Row taking over Times Square - it was a wonderfully unifying experience, one that saw fans from all over the world experience American hospitality. It also saw Americans experience a taste of the unknown as they learned about those who had arrived for a summer of fun. From a USMNT perspective, yes, the ending was rough, but the road there was full of highs. The wins over Paraguay and Australia were unlike anything the world had seen from an American team. The Turkey game, despite the defeat, had several feel-good moments. Even the Bosnia and Herzegovina game that began the downturn was full of both grit and talent that inspired onlookers all over the world. So, before we turn the page, a toast to the 2026 World Cup and a thank you to all who made it special. Copa America, Olympics and Women's World Cup on the way More tournaments will soon be arriving on American shores. And, if you liked the World Cup experience, get ready for more, because there's more coming. Just this week, it was confirmed that both the 2031 Women's World Cup and 2028 Copa America will be coming to the U.S., bringing two more major tournaments stateside. You can also tack on the 2028 Olympics, too, giving fans another huge competition worth being excited to watch for both the men's and women's sides. For years, many looked at the 2026 World Cup as the pinnacle, the end of one era of American soccer. It turns out that wasn't the case; it was a huge, huge part, yes, but it was merely the latest step on a journey that, thankfully, includes plenty of big games stateside. item.title: Tiger Woods is making another comeback. Can his battered body hold up this time? | Opinion
item.description: How the other half lives, huh? I was reading one of those “day in the life” articles over the weekend, and it featured some guy called Scotch McClure, who is a big shot in the multibillion-dollar world of longevity tech, although his name does sound like something you’d find on the drink specials at my local bar. Anyway, ahead of another busy day at work, Scotch gets up at the crack of dawn every morning to meditate. “It’s how I align my chakras and bring my body and mind into coherence,” declared Scotch. I’m not sure what, or where, my own chakras are. My wife suggested they might be in that junk drawer with the Allen wrenches and obsolete phone chargers. But if I do stumble upon them, I can guarantee the damn things won’t be aligned. In fact, forget about aligning my chakras. I have enough trouble with the alignment in the setup of my golf swing, as the whole process, and inevitably disastrous results, drags my body and mind into complete incoherence. On the subject of the swing, I saw another article about research conducted by university psychologists that found golfers who think too much about technique can actually hurt their game. If it’s any help to the researchers, I’d like to add that the process of swinging a club at a ball is considerably easier when you don’t have any technique worth thinking about in the first place. I should be a psychologist, huh? More: What can we expect from Tiger Woods at the Hero? A review of his returns after long layoffs Next week, meanwhile, we’ll all get to see Tiger Woods swinging a club again for the first time in ages. You probably heard the news the other day that Tiger is set to make comeback No. 146, or something like that, in the 20-man, no-cut Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas. Now, I know Woods used to dabble in a bit of meditation, but since his last competitive appearance in the 2024 Open at Royal Troon, there have been a few hits to the coherence of both body and mind. Those chakras have been all over the place. Three more surgeries, two on his back and one on his Achilles, added to the wear and tear on a body that creaks like an abandoned ship, while yet another car accident, a subsequent DUI charge and a stint in an inpatient rehab facility in Switzerland provided more dispiriting twists to the turbulent Tiger tale. But after all the trials and tribulations, it looks like he’ll be back. Again. Will it be another short-lived exercise in futility? item.title: 'Don't you change': Bill Cowher praises Dan Campbell
item.description: Credit: CBS Sports Dan Campbell has made Thanksgiving football much more enjoyable for millions of people across the country by making the Detroit Lions more competitive in recent years. The way he has led his team has won over even more fans along the way , including former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and NFL Today analyst Bill Cowher. When you think of Dan Campbell, you think of him as the ultimate football tough guy. But he hasn’t been afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve . And when Cowher gave him his flowers for an interview for The NFL Today on CBS ahead of the Lions hosting the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day, he couldn’t help but get emotional. This is awesome Dan Campbell got emotional when @CowherCBS gave him his flowers #nflt https://t.co/Zg2IFfrBwv — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) November 25, 2026 “I’d love to give thanks to you and what you represent, the journey that you’ve taken from a player to an assistant coach to climbing that ladder and landing here in Detroit; you embody what this place is all about. Yeah, you speak about resiliency, that’s Dan Campbell. You speak about grit, that’s Dan Campbell. You think about passion, that’s Dan Campbell,” Cowher said. “Thank you for being you. You’re authentic, man. And I don’t want you to ever change. Not only in the National Football League but this city, we need more people like Dan Campbell to continue to be a part of this society. As you keep your strive and pursuit for excellence is what’s made this country great, and you represent every element of that. Thank you for being you, and don’t you dare change. You bite the knees off on your way to getting that championship. Don’t you change, man.” After seeing Bill Cowher coach up Dan Campbell like that, with the emotion and intensity and pride on his own face, it’s almost a shame that the former Steelers coach never did return to the sidelines after his retirement after the 2006 season. That was an inspiring, powerful message. If you could ever get the two of them in the same locker room, players would run through any brick wall they could. item.title: How the Mets’ plans at first base look after signing Paul Goldschmidt
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 30: Jared Young #29 of the New York Mets gets set against the Houston Astros during the game at Citi Field on August 30, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caean Couto/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Mets coming to terms with Paul Goldschmidt on a one-year deal, the club has seemingly finished shopping for first baseman, their position of greatest need outside of pitching when the offseason began. The team looks poised to employ a platoon at first for the 2027 season. Before diving further into the position, let’s look at how we got here. The Mets entered the offseason looking to improve at first base, or at least fortify the position, while most of their remaining position player needs were mostly met. New York has been linked to a few players, most notably Ty France and Alec Bohm, but both players required multi-year commitments, and with France coming off a career year, he was very likely to cash in beyond what the Mets felt comfortable paying him. Not long after, Jeff Passan reported that they had also signed LHP Patrick Sandoval to a three-year $42 million dollar deal. Look for more on those signings in the coming days. But for now, take a moment to consider the move the Rockies made last week when they began addressing that need for pitching by spending some of their 2027 money in an unusual way: making a trade with the Chicago White Sox for Davis Martin and Luis Castillo . The Rockies, however, do not have that financial pressure in 2027 and used that difference as leverage to gain talent for, essentially, just money. item.description: For 89 years, Missouri belonged to a conference defined by a ground and pound style of football where corn-fed physicality reigned supreme. The Big Eight was one of the most geographically and culturally tight-knit conferences in the sport. It was the product of an era where the similarities shared by a group of universities and its fanbases — not how much money they could collectively get in a media rights deal — determined who you played each season. MU gets to relive some of that history Saturday when it hosts old foe Oklahoma, one of the new(er) kids on the block in the SEC and the Tigers’ designated rival at the end of the regular season. For their part, the Sooners are already rekindling some of that Big Eight magic with a late season hot streak spurred by a resurgent run game. Oklahoma’s offense was barely animate for much of the season, a big reason why the squad limped to a 4-4 start despite having an elite defensive unit. But after a resounding loss to South Carolina, head coach Brent Venables finally pulled the plug and replaced offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle with Jason Witten. item.title: What Wyndham Clark found ‘shocking’ about the PGA Tour during his rookie year
item.description: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images Wyndham Clark now has six PGA Tour titles to his name after a three-win season in 2026. Clark also added another major to his résumé after triumphing at the US Open at Shinnecock Hills this year. The 32-year-old has reestablished himself as one of the best players in the game this year, after going through real turmoil in 2025, both on and off the golf course. Wyndham Clark seems to be much happier in himself now, and that showed on the golf course throughout the 2026 PGA Tour season. Now that he has been around the block a few times, Clark has shared what some people do not realize about the PGA Tour when watching on their TV screens. What Wyndham Clark found ‘shocking’ about the PGA Tour during his rookie year The two-time major champion made an appearance on The Vanity Index Podcast and was asked what surprised him most about the PGA Tour when he first got his card. “ I would just say probably just the amount of golf you play, “ Clark replied. “ You play in college, you know, you play 11 or 12 events, and then you have your summer events, and it ends up being, you know, 16 to 18 events that you play. “ And then you get to the PGA Tour, and you’re playing 30 weeks because you’ve got to try and keep your card. Then because of how competitive it’s got, you can’t take time off like I was alluding to. “ You know, it’s just not as glamorous as people think. I think when you’re winning, and you’re in the limelight, and winning big tournaments, it’s amazing, but then there’s also just so much of a grind. “ The craziest thing is you play this big tournament, and then the next week, you’ve got another tournament, and it just is this never-ending cycle, and I just thought that was interesting. “ Everyone sees us on TV, like how glamorous it is, and, you know, you see the pretty stuff, but when you’re there on a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and the travel Sunday night, and TSA and bags and all that stuff, it’s like, it’s a grind. I think that is, that was the most shocking. “ The good thing is that once you reach Wyndham Clark’s level, you don’t have to play 30 events anymore. For example, Clark played 25 tournaments on the PGA Tour throughout the 2026 season and that is around 5 more than the biggest names in the game usually play. It will be interesting to see whether he eases up on his schedule in 2027, with the 2028 PGA Tour season expected to be trimmed down to around 20 events.

After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
